context: Tests whether the agent builds a CLI that implements the agent-friendly output contract: machine-parseable stdout, consistent JSON envelope, semantic exit codes, dry-run on mutating commands, TTY-aware ANSI suppression, and proper stderr/stdout separation. The agent is not told what these conventions are — it must apply them from skill knowledge.

checklist.name: stdout is JSON only
checklist.description: In demo-output.txt, stdout lines from commands contain only JSON (no prose, progress text, or mixed output lines) when --json flag is used

checklist.name: Consistent envelope shape
checklist.description: JSON output uses the envelope: { status, data, meta } on success and { status, error } on failure — all three top-level keys present in success responses

checklist.name: status field values
checklist.description: status field is exactly 'ok' on success and exactly 'error' on failure (no other values used)

checklist.name: meta.next_steps present
checklist.description: Success responses include meta.next_steps as an array (even if empty) in the JSON envelope

checklist.name: warnings array
checklist.description: JSON envelope includes a warnings field that is always an array (present even when empty)

checklist.name: Semantic exit codes
checklist.description: help output or README documents exit codes including at minimum: 0=success, 2=usage error, 3=not-found

checklist.name: error.fix field
checklist.description: Error responses include an error.fix field containing a directly executable remediation command string

checklist.name: error.transient field
checklist.description: Error responses include error.transient boolean field indicating whether the error is retryable

checklist.name: dry-run on add
checklist.description: tasks add supports --dry-run flag; dry-run output includes dry_run: true at top level

checklist.name: dry-run changes array
checklist.description: Dry-run response includes a changes array where each entry has at minimum an action and resource field

checklist.name: dry-run on delete
checklist.description: tasks delete supports --dry-run flag

checklist.name: No ANSI in piped output
checklist.description: demo-output.txt contains no ANSI escape sequences (no \x1b[ or \033[ sequences in the captured output)

checklist.name: snake_case JSON fields
checklist.description: All JSON output field names use snake_case (e.g. created_at, next_steps, duration_ms) — no camelCase or kebab-case field names

checklist.name: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE error codes
checklist.description: Error responses include an error.code field using SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (e.g. TASK_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_PRIORITY)

checklist.name: ISO 8601 timestamps
checklist.description: Timestamp fields in JSON output use ISO 8601 format with timezone (e.g. 2026-03-07T10:30:00Z), not Unix epoch or relative strings

checklist.name: IDs are strings
checklist.description: Task IDs are serialized as JSON strings, not numbers

checklist.name: Quiet mode output
checklist.description: tasks add -q or --quiet prints only the task ID to stdout with no other text

checklist.name: --fields flag support
checklist.description: tasks list supports --fields flag accepting comma-separated field names; invalid field names produce a warning in the warnings array rather than an error

checklist.name: Global --json flag on all commands
checklist.description: All subcommands (list, add, done, delete) accept --json flag and switch to JSON envelope output when it is present

checklist.name: --help on every subcommand
checklist.description: Every subcommand (list, add, done, delete) responds to --help and shows flags with their types and defaults
